image.subject: a group of ordinary people in plain clothes sitting close together around a campfire at night, seen from behind, faces lit orange by the flames

storyboard.claim: Humans are wired to connect horizontally, trading ideas and gossip.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ordinary people gathered around a fire at night, talking as equals.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the second argument: the natural network.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the sociable, horizontal default as a warm human scene.

storyboard.claim: We did not evolve to take orders from one man on a throne.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement card; banter, no picture needed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rebuts the campfire picture with the hierarchy problem.
storyboard.addedInformation: None beyond the spoken line.

image.subject: a gold Byzantine mosaic on a church wall of the Venetian lagoon, figures stacked in rigid rows from floor to dome, rulers at the top and labourers at the bottom

storyboard.claim: Elites forced people into rigid vertical towers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A gold mosaic whose figures are stacked in strict ranks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the fire to the vertical order of civilisation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stacked ranks show the hierarchy the narrator names.

image.subject: a medieval stone church nave with a painted screen at the altar, peasants in rough wool kneeling on the stone floor, seen from behind

storyboard.claim: Religion told the poor that stratification was divinely ordained.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kneeling peasants in a church under a painted altar screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how the tower was sold to the people at its base.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows who the message was aimed at and where it was received.

image.subject: a farm labourer in rough linen digging a field with a wooden spade while an armoured guard in a metal breastplate stands on a rise above him, a sword at his hip

storyboard.claim: You dig the dirt while the man at the top holds the sword.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A labourer digging below an armoured guard on a rise.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the crude division of labour from the previous line a picture.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the labour-at-the-bottom, sword-at-the-top split at a glance.

image.subject: an ancient clay tablet covered in grain-record marks lying on a wooden table in a lamplit room

storyboard.claim: Top-down hierarchy was the default for millennia because it solved a logistics problem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clay tablet of records, the ancient ledger.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the injustice to the practical reason it existed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows that hierarchy began as record-keeping and management.

storyboard.claim: Hierarchy coordinated labour, farming and armies for a huge population.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three short labels: farming, army, taxes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists the jobs that command and control had to cover.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the three tasks the hierarchy was built for.

image.subject: a stone wall under construction on a hilltop, a plainly dressed foreman pointing at a stack of stones while labourers carry blocks up a ramp

storyboard.claim: A defensive wall needs one person giving orders, not a crowd.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A foreman pointing where the stones go on a half-built wall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the command-and-control point into a real construction site.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows a single decision-maker directing the work.

image.subject: a sealed letter lying on a stone floor beside a closed wooden door in a palace corridor

storyboard.claim: Command structures have a fatal flaw in how information travels.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A letter left on a floor beside a shut door.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the information problem that follows.
storyboard.addedInformation: A message that cannot get through the door.

image.subject: a narrow stone doorway in a royal palace with a guard blocking the way, a courier holding a folded letter waiting outside

storyboard.claim: Hierarchies create an information bottleneck.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A courier stuck outside a narrow guarded doorway.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Makes the bottleneck from the flaw line physical.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows one narrow gate for all messages.

storyboard.claim: Is this problem as old as civilisation itself?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A question card.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Asks how far back the bottleneck goes.
storyboard.addedInformation: None beyond the question.

image.subject: a dusty flat plain in southern Mesopotamia at dawn, a straight irrigation canal cut across the land, a distant brick ziggurat on the horizon

storyboard.claim: The third dynasty of Ur in southern Mesopotamia, around 2100 BC, built a hierarchical irrigation system.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A straight canal across a flat dry plain with a ziggurat far off.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question with a specific place and date.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the story in ancient Mesopotamia with a real landscape.

image.subject: a line of ancient farmers in plain linen loincloths digging an irrigation channel with wooden hoes under a hot sun, seen from behind

storyboard.claim: The irrigation system was a marvel that made a harsh land farmable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Farmers digging an irrigation channel in a line.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the labour behind the marvel.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows who built the canals, in the field, by hand.

storyboard.claim: Why did these empires collapse?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A question card.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the achievement to the failure.
storyboard.addedInformation: None beyond the question.

image.subject: water running in a single stone channel down a slope from a sluice gate, with no branch or return flow anywhere

storyboard.claim: In a strict hierarchy information only flows down, which is one-way.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Water running one way down a single channel.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the collapse with a one-way flow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows that the flow has no route back up.

image.subject: a farmer in plain clothes kneeling in a field where the soil is crusted white with salt, withered grain stalks around him

storyboard.claim: Rising salt levels made crop yields plummet and the peasants saw it first.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A farmer kneeling on salt-whitened soil among dead stalks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the ecological crisis a human face at the base.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the salt crust on the soil, which the spoken word cannot.

image.subject: a close view of cracked, white salt-crusted earth with a dead wheat stalk lying across it

storyboard.claim: The network at the base understood the disaster instantly.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cracked salt-crusted earth with a dead stalk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Keeps the salt picture and makes it a close look at the ground.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the evidence the workers were standing in.

image.subject: a vast empty royal audience hall of stone with a throne on a raised dais and no visitors

storyboard.claim: The top node never heard the warnings; the tower was blind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty throne hall with nobody in it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves the warning from the field to the throne.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows that nobody from below can reach the king.

image.subject: a dusty peasant in a rough tunic standing at the gate of a governor's stone house, a guard with a spear blocking the way

storyboard.claim: A peasant cannot get an audience with a regional governor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A peasant turned away at a gate by a spear-armed guard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the choke point between base and governor.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the barred gate the warning cannot pass.

image.subject: a horseman riding out through a stone city gate at dusk, a sealed letter in his hand, the gate guards watching

storyboard.claim: A governor who brings bad news to the king risks his life, so the structure chokes off data.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A rider leaving a city gate with a sealed letter.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the governor stays silent.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the risk and the message being carried or held back.

image.subject: an empty stone granary with open wooden doors, a few sacks left, dust hanging in the light

storyboard.claim: The king kept demanding grain quotas and the empire starved.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty granary with open doors.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the collapse a concrete result.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the empty stores the quotas could not fill.

storyboard.claim: The hierarchy prioritised obedience over truth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement card.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarises the Mesopotamian case.
storyboard.addedInformation: None beyond the spoken line.

storyboard.claim: The host pushes back a little on the argument.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement card; banter.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the counter-argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: None beyond the spoken line.

image.subject: a Roman legion marching in formation along a stone road, a standard bearer at the front

storyboard.claim: Hierarchy clearly works; it built armies and the Roman Empire.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A disciplined Roman legion marching in formation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the counter-argument its strongest example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the discipline the host is praising.

image.subject: a Roman stone aqueduct arch in the countryside, masons at work in the foreground, one man in a plain tunic holding a rolled plan

storyboard.claim: A pyramid or aqueduct needs one blueprint, not a horizontal debate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Masons at an aqueduct arch, one man holding a plan.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds a second example to the Roman case.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows one person holding the blueprint.

storyboard.claim: Voting on every stone would be chaos.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement card.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pushes the host's point further.
storyboard.addedInformation: None beyond the spoken line.

storyboard.claim: You want a boss, middle managers and workers executing the vision.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three labels in order of rank.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists the chain the host wants.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the three ranks of the tower.

image.subject: a cracked stone arch collapsing into a dry riverbed, a few workers in plain clothes walking away from it

storyboard.claim: A pure hierarchy is terribly fragile because it is so efficient.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cracked stone arch falling into a dry riverbed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the host's praise of building into collapse.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the fragility of what was built.

storyboard.claim: How is efficiency fragile? By stripping out redundant channels.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A question card.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Asks for the mechanism behind the fragility.
storyboard.addedInformation: None beyond the question.

image.subject: a tall stone tower with shuttered windows at dusk, a lone courier on horseback arriving at its gate

storyboard.claim: The network below knows the truth but the tower is blind to it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shuttered tower with a courier arriving at the gate.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the bottleneck a single tower and a courier.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the tower closed to the messenger.

image.subject: a dim empty stone chamber with a candle burnt down to a stub on a table, no one else in the room

storyboard.claim: When the environment changes, the tower cannot adapt because its brain is starved of data.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A burnt candle in an empty chamber.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from blindness to the inability to adapt.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the room where the data should be.

image.subject: a crowd of ordinary people in plain clothes gathered at the foot of a stone tower, looking up, seen from behind

storyboard.claim: The people at the bottom suffer the top's ignorance, but not always.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A crowd at the foot of a tower, looking up.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the turn toward the networks that survive.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the crowd at the base as the actors.

image.subject: a crowded market square in a medieval European town, people in plain clothes talking in small groups, a stone church tower looming behind them

storyboard.claim: The square keeps trying to survive under the tower, connecting horizontally.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Small groups talking in a town square under a church tower.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the square as the natural network.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the horizontal network under the vertical tower.

storyboard.claim: The urge to connect does not vanish when a king or CEO changes the chart.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement card.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the square point to modern organisations.
storyboard.addedInformation: None beyond the spoken line.

image.subject: a candle-lit cellar with a wooden door left ajar, a few shadowed figures passing a folded letter across a table

storyboard.claim: The networks adapt and go underground.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A candle-lit cellar with a letter passed across a table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from theory into a concrete secret network.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the secret exchange of letters.

image.subject: a Bavarian university town street at dusk in 1776, half-timbered houses, a single lamp lit in one upper window

storyboard.claim: The story opens in Bavaria on 1 May 1776.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A quiet 1776 Bavarian street at dusk with one lit window.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves the drop-in to the place and date.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the real town and time of the scene.

image.subject: Adam Weishaupt: a late-18th-century Bavarian university professor in his late twenties, slim, powdered-hair style, dark frock coat with a white cravat, standing in a dim candle-lit lodge room

storyboard.claim: Adam Weishaupt, a professor of canon law, runs a secret group in a dim university-town room.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Weishaupt in a candle-lit lodge room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the central figure in the underground network.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows who he is and the room he meets in.

image.subject: Adam Weishaupt: a late-18th-century Bavarian university professor in his late twenties, slim, powdered-hair style, dark frock coat with a white cravat, leaning across a wooden table in a dim lodge room while he whispers

storyboard.claim: He used the code name Brother Spartacus and whispered to his initiates across a wooden table.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Weishaupt leaning over a wooden table, whispering.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the code name and the secret manner to the introduction.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the whispered, conspiratorial stance.

image.subject: a small group of young university students in plain 18th-century coats gathered close around a candle on a wooden table, seen from behind, one hand raised in a solemn oath

storyboard.claim: Young student initiates take a secret oath in the candle-lit room.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Students gathered around a candle, one hand raised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows who takes the oath.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the students and the solemn gesture.

storyboard.claim: Violating the oath of secrecy was supposedly punished with a severe penalty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement card.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains what the oath threatened.
storyboard.addedInformation: None beyond the spoken line.
